configuration: make -C epoch3d COMPILER=gfortran, then the single lehe_x deck of code/epoch/epoch3d/tests/maxwell_solvers, unchanged from upstream except for the explicit rank layout nprocx = 2, nprocy = 2, nprocz = 1 and the added bz output; nx = 240, ny = nx/3 = 80, nz = ny = 80 cells over x, y and z in [-12, 12] micron on each axis, t_end = 75 fs, dt_snapshot = 25 fs, so 4 dumps at the upstream cadence; 4 MPI ranks. Graded: Ey and Bz of every dump, 8 raw float64 files of 252 x 92 x 92 = 2132928 values each (the 240 x 80 x 80 grid plus the 6-cell CPML layer at each end of every axis), 130 MB in total. The knobs SAB_NX, SAB_TEND_FS and the rank layout reach other resolutions and windows; the defaults above are the upstream values.
observable: Ey and Bz of all 4 dumps of the lehe_x deck, 252 x 92 x 92 cells each, as raw float64
default_vs_upstream: cells, window and cadence upstream; 4 ranks (2 x 2 x 1) where the upstream makefile runs 2, a decomposition the field solve is bitwise invariant under; SAB_NPROCY=1 restores 2
variant: the laser block's intensity_w_cm2 multiplied by (1 + 1e-15), 1.0e15 becoming 1.000000000000001e15. EPOCH turns that intensity into the field amplitude with a square root (epoch3d/src/deck/deck_laser_block.f90:120-135), so the driven amplitude moves by 5e-16 relative, between two and three double ulps: far too small to be physics and far too large for rounding to eat. Measured natively on this deck, the perturbation reaches 65 per cent of the 17 063 424 graded values and moves them by at most 7.25e-04 V/m and 7.39e-13 T, so the variant genuinely changes the graded output and its distance from the nominal run is the floor this policy sits above. A different MPI rank layout would NOT be a usable variant here: the halo exchange is a pure MPI_SENDRECV of subarrays with no arithmetic (epoch3d/src/boundary.F90), so the field solve is bitwise invariant under the decomposition and the two runs would come back identical.

evidence.floor_how: Two-build floor, measured on this deck: the pinned source built with the makefile's gfortran profile (-O3 -g -std=f2003) and, in a second copy, with that one line changed to -O2, both run on ic/nominal at the graded settings; largest absolute difference over the 8 graded files: 6.447e-04 V/m on the electric-field files and 6.537e-13 T on the magnetic-field files. Variant preview: the -O3 build on ic/variant against ic/nominal, largest absolute difference 7.2479e-04 V/m and 7.3896e-13 T, differing in 65 per cent of the 17 063 424 graded values. Wrong-answer probe, made on the 1-D optimized stencil deck with one binary so that only the deck changed: multiplying its deltax coefficient by (1 + 1e-9), (1 + 1e-6) and (1 + 1e-3) moves Ey by 3.19e+02, 3.19e+05 and 3.19e+08 V/m and Bz by 8.02e-07, 8.02e-04 and 8.02e-01 T, exactly linear in the coefficient error, so this bound is crossed by any stencil coefficient wrong by more than about 3e-12 relative. This check's own run.sh, rubric.json and validate.py were run end to end natively on both initial conditions and the pair passes, with the worst graded value at 7.25e-04 of its bound. All of it was run natively on the authoring machine (macOS 14 arm64, gfortran 15, OpenMPI 5, 4 ranks, SAB_MAKE_JOBS=4); the in-container spread is written later by selfcheck.
evidence.expected_runtime_derivation: shipped calibration record 20260902T155717Z on the x86 worker (8 cpus, 8 GB): this check ran 12.5 s, with its 66 s source build recorded separately and outside the suite budget. expected_runtime_s is a declaration carrying headroom over that measurement, not the measurement itself; the next selfcheck rewrites it.

warrant: The graded observable is the transverse electric field Ey and the transverse magnetic field Bz of every one of the 4 dumps of the lehe_x deck of the upstream maxwell_solvers test in 3-D -- a 1e15 W/cm2, 0.5 micron gaussian laser pulse crossing 24 microns of vacuum in 75 fs -- written by the pinned code at full double precision and compared value by value with an absolute bound of 1 V/m on the electric-field files and 3.34e-09 T on the magnetic-field files and no relative term. The two numbers are one bound: the arrays are in strict SI and a vacuum wave carries |B| = |E|/c, which the source shows directly in the coefficients of the two sweeps, hdt/dx*c**2 on the B differences that update E against hdt/dx on the E differences that update B (epoch3d/src/fields.f90), and the magnetic bound 3.34e-09 T is the electric one, 1 V/m, divided by the speed of light. What this deck puts under test: maxwell_solver = lehe_x in three dimensions, where the B sweep reaches thirty-six multiplies and a hundred and twenty additions per cell per half step (epoch3d/src/fields.f90:655-733). lehe_y and lehe_z are never selected by any upstream deck, so this is the only orientation of the family the task can hold a port to. Physical: the stencil coefficients alpha, beta, gamma and delta enter a run only through update_b_field -- update_e_field is always the plain centred difference -- and their entire purpose is to set the group velocity of exactly this pulse, which is what the upstream test measures and accepts to 0.022 relative. That was probed rather than argued: multiplying the deltax coefficient of the 1-D optimized stencil deck by (1 + 1e-9), a coefficient still correct to nine significant figures, moves Ey by 319 V/m and Bz by 8.0e-07 T over the same window, 319 and 240 times this bound, and the response is exactly linear in the coefficient error, so a coefficient wrong in its third figure gives 3.2e+08 V/m. Dropping one beta term, or leaving alpha at 1 instead of deriving it from the others, breaks the unit sum of the stencil and changes the field by of order the pulse amplitude itself, 1e11 V/m. Achievable: the field update is a fixed-length sum of products with no iteration, no interpolation table, no reduction and no OpenMP anywhere in fields.f90, so two legitimate runs of the pinned source can differ only by floating-point association and by the last ulp of the intrinsics the coefficients are built from -- the SIN that builds the Lehe delta coefficient and the SQRT that turns the deck's intensity into a field amplitude (epoch3d/src/deck/deck_laser_block.f90:120-135) -- and a single ulp there perturbs every cell of all ~240 steps. Measured natively on this deck: the -O3 and the -O2 build of the pinned source differ over the graded files by 6.447e-04 V/m on the electric-field files and 6.537e-13 T on the magnetic-field files, and the variant, a 1e-15 relative perturbation of the deck's laser intensity, grows over the window to 7.2479e-04 V/m and 7.3896e-13 T. The bound therefore sits about 1380 times above the largest legitimate spread measured natively on this deck, which is 6.96e-15 of the field amplitude, and leaves an accelerated implementation -- one that reassociates every stencil sum, contracts multiplies and adds into FMAs, and brings its own libm -- three to four orders of magnitude of room, while still sitting more than two orders below the smallest coefficient fault probed and eleven below a realistic one. Absolute rather than relative because the arrays cross zero twice per wavelength and the difference between two runs is largest where the field is largest, not where it is small.
